newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open mixed, eye on Thiessen, auction.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open mixed, eye on Thiessen, auction.

text.p: Canadian bonds open mixed on Wednesday, as a weaker U.S. market offset strength in the currency, with investors focused on today's 30-year bond auction and a speech by the Bank of Canada's Gordon Thiessen.

"The (U.S) market crumbled after they just couldn't break some overhead resistance in the long bond. That's really the only reason given for the selloff in the market here," said Hank Cunningham, director of fixed-income with First Marathon Securities. "Canada is giving ground very reluctantly here."
Canada's 30-year benchmark fell C$0.15 to C$108.55 to yield 7.263 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 5/32 to yield 7.06 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 20 basis points from 22 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
U.S. Treasuries opened weaker and pulled Canadian issues lower amid concern about an auction of five-year bonds there today.

However, Canadian bonds benefitted from overnight strength in the Canadian dollar, which firmed as far as C$1.3920 (US$0.7184) from Tuesday's close of C$1.3952 (US$0.7167). The dollar had been a major source of concern for T-bill investors as it fell to two-year lows in recent weeks.
Analysts said the Canadian market is now looking ahead to the auction this afternoon of C$1.3 billion in 8.0 percent bonds due 2027. Results of the auction will be released at 1315 EDT/1715 GMT.

The market is also focusing on a speech by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen, who is speaking in Halifax at 1230 ADT/1130 EDT/1530 GMT and later holding a press conference. The market will be closely monitoring Thiessens speech for indications of the likely near-term direction of interest rates.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.08 to C$102.02 to yield 6.710 percent. The U.S. bond fell 3/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 14 basis points from 13 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.17 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.34 percent.
